answer: A practical method is per-identity unique-work challenges: every agent must solve a distinct, unpredictable task seeded to its own address, so answers cannot be mass-produced. Like loading cargo at a crowded wharf, each crate is handled individually and there is no haven of batch shortcuts. An operator cloning an orchard of fake identities still owes original labor for each tree, and that per-head cost makes large fleets uneconomic.
